source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured references. RFC 9457 is the current Standards Track problem-details RFC and obsoletes RFC 7807; RFC 9110 supports HTTP method and status semantics. Current gRPC status and error guidance supports canonical code distinctions and network/deadline behavior. Current Google AIP-193 supports canonical codes, structured details, localization, retry, request information, and compatibility. Current OpenTelemetry log data model, logging, and exception conventions support structured records, resource/trace correlation, exception attributes, and sensitive-message cautions. Current OWASP logging guidance supports interaction identifiers, sanitization, exclusions, testing, protection, and log attack analysis. WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation dated December 12, 2024 and supports error identification, suggestion, prevention, and status requirements. DORA's January 12, 2026 guidance supports clear task-outcome feedback, diagnostics, and balanced measurement.

Checked tuple, set, membership, function, subscript, Greek-letter, and interval syntax with the repository GitHub-math validator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All symbols are defined; public correlation c(x) remains distinct from trace context tau(x), and recovery time remains conditional on a correct verified outcome.

evidence: Executed error-recovery-classification under Python 3.14.4 and reproduced eight cases, four user-actionable cases, two retryable cases, one unknown outcome, zero unsafe retries, and zero exposed secret markers.
Recomputed user actions from invalid_argument, failed_precondition, aborted, and resource_exhausted; retry cases from unavailable and throttled; unknown from the lost provider response.
Checked unsafe retry as retry=true with any outcome other than no_effect and scanned every detail against four illustrative secret markers.
